notes.subject: language
notes.text: Hangul: a unique script where many letters contain circles, unlike other East Asian writing.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: Poles nearly always wear black and yellow diagonal stripes low down; the stripes stop above the ground and look truly yellow.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: Most utility poles end in a tapered spike at the top.

notes.subject: plate
notes.text: Newer plates are white (private) or yellow (commercial), long or short; older ones are short and green.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Blue house-shaped address plates show the full address in the local script and in Latin letters.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Blue arrow-shaped street name signs hang from metal bars on utility poles.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Pedestrian crossing sign is a blue pentagon.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Warning triangles have a yellow background, while prohibition and yield signs are white.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Direction signs show white text on green.

notes.subject: line
notes.text: Yellow centre line with white edge lines; red block markings sometimes appear on the road.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Traffic drives on the right.

notes.subject: bollard
notes.text: Black and white wedge-shaped bollards with a yellow round reflector at the front and a grey one at the back.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Speed bumps are often painted yellow and white.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Mostly mountainous; even flat areas show hills on the horizon.

notes.subject: architecture
notes.text: Red brick is a very common building material, and many roofs are blue.

notes.subject: architecture
notes.text: Traditional tiled roofs with decorative corners and sides that curve slightly upward.

notes.subject: car
notes.text: Nearly all coverage is Generation 3, usually with the rear of a black, white and silver car visible; never an antenna.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: A lot of coverage is autumn and winter, though spring and summer exists too.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Area codes rise toward the south, from the capital's two-digit code up to 064 on the southern island.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Dark volcanic soil, volcano views and black rock walls mark the southern island.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: One of the few totally flat areas, with open yellow-green fields along the roads.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: House numbers with a big white section at the top identify this area.

notes.subject: car
notes.text: Older Generation 2 coverage is almost only in the two biggest cities.
